tasks.short: Help site managers cost a choice and put the budget together.

today.trigger: The budget calendar opens, or a site manager, the Controller or the Finance Director asks what a cost split or a next-year envelope should look like.
steps: Pull site actuals and the current forecast from the nightly AFAS extract into a personal Excel file.
Sit with Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo and split labour, CAO overtime, agency flex, housing, transport and overhead.
Rebuild the allocation so the cost centres add up to the site and the company.
Draft the assumptions in Excel or a mail and walk the open points with the Controller.
drudgery: Re-keying AFAS numbers into personal workbooks each cycle.
Asking three sites for the same drivers: hours, agency rate and volume.
Rewriting the allocation note so the totals agree.
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes into assembling a workbook the manager will change again, and into repeating the same driver conversation.

lenses.faster: Pulling the actuals and rebuilding the standard cost split disappear. The meeting with the site manager stays about an hour, plus a short check of the drivers, so about a third of the hours on this task disappear.
lenses.autonomous: The budget calendar or a Teams request opens a pack of actuals, drivers and gaps. The pack is assembled without the analyst, and the analyst checks the drivers before any option is treated as advice.
lenses.ambitious: A fresh set of costed flex options for the three site managers during peak, when agency use moves between 150 and 300 people, would be a new service they do not get between annual budgets. Demand would grow if a new option set was cheap, because volume moves every few weeks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying AFAS into Excel and reformatting the allocation. The analyst wants more of the conversation about which cost the site can actually move.
lenses.options: An overtime mix, an agency-flex mix and a lower-volume mix produce different labour costs under the CAO and the agency rate. Which mix is affordable changes the envelope the site asks for.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward site conversations on a small set of drivers the analyst maintains. They gain the right to say which driver definition the forecast uses, with the Finance Director still accepting the budget. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The Controller’s first-pass reading of a site budget submission. The analyst would need the Controller’s materiality limits and the variances the Finance Director asks about every cycle.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which site pads the agency line, which overtime is structural, and what the works council will challenge. That judgement belongs in the meeting, and the analyst has to choose the option the company will stand behind.
tasks.pattern_why: The product is advice in a conversation, and the analyst stays the lead. A fixed calculation can cost the options, but it cannot decide which option to put in front of a site manager.

in_practice.trigger: A date on the budget calendar, or a Teams request from a site manager or the Controller.
steps: A workbook opens on the nightly AFAS extract with actuals, the current forecast and the standard drivers per site.
The analyst selects two or three mixes the site can actually run, and the sheet costs each one.
The analyst edits the assumption note and uses it in the meeting.
The chosen mix and the rejected mixes are saved with the driver set that produced them.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs the note before it goes to the site or the Controller. The Finance Director still accepts the budget.
data_needed: Cost-centre actuals and the current forecast
Volume and hours by site
CAO overtime parameters and the agency rate card
Allocation rules
Headcount by role and site, held as aggregates
in_practice.logs_to: The versioned note and driver set in the SharePoint budget folder, kept with the month’s forecast file so an auditor can rebuild it.

evidence.claim: In a survey of 2,000 finance executives, budgeting was the task where AI most often beat expectations, a net score of +42.
OneStream describes FP&A agents as doing the mechanics while people decide capital allocation and face the board.
Speed without defined drivers and encoded policies repeats rollover budgets, padding and silo plans.
At Noordhaven this public-sector task is cost-centre and site budget advice, read with the board and the bank in view.

risks: A rolled-over site budget can come back as fluent advice and hide last year’s padding.
Named people in a headcount plan are personal data under the AVG, so the working file has to stay on roles, hours and cost.
A cheaper labour mix can be a works-council matter under the CAO, and finance advice is then ahead of the consultation.
Power BI Copilot can misread an unprepared model, and non-English use is not officially supported, so the costing sheet should be a fixed model with Dutch cost-centre names.
research_questions: How many hours in a budget cycle do the two analysts spend assembling workbooks, and how many sitting with the three site managers?
Are labour, flex, overtime and volume drivers written down once and used in AFAS, Power BI and the site sheets?
Which labour-mix choices need works-council advice or consent before they can be presented as the plan?
Does the Finance Director change the envelope when shown two costed mixes?

tasks.short: Review site budgets for trends that change what they will need.

today.trigger: The nightly extract refreshes after month end, or a site’s volume, absence or agency use moves off the plan during the month.
steps: Export budget versus actual by site from Power BI into Excel.
Compare hours, overtime, agency flex, transport and warehouse cost for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo over recent months.
Ask the site or a bookkeeper why a material line moved.
Write a trend note for the Controller and update what the forecast needs next quarter.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same twelve-month trend table.
Copying last month’s comments forward.
Reconciling agency-portal hours to the AFAS labour accounts.
today.time_sinks: Waiting on an explanation that is often the same driver as last month, and cleaning lines that do not tie to the ledger.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the trend table and the first sourced note disappears. Reading the few variances that change next quarter’s need, and one conversation with the site when the note is thin, stays at about an hour a site. About half the hours on this task disappear.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly refresh after month end starts the review. The tie-out and the draft note run without the analyst. The analyst approves the note before the forecast need changes.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly decision on next-quarter budget need for each site, including the flex band, would replace the once-a-year company trend. Demand would grow if that decision was cheap, because volume and absence move every month.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the pivot. The analyst wants more time on the few trends that should change a driver.
lenses.options: Flat volume, the customer’s stated peak, and a high-absence case give different flex and overtime needs for a site such as Tilburg. The case the analyst accepts changes the forecast need.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a review of driver breaches. The analyst gains the right to propose a change to the flex or overtime driver before the quarterly forecast, and the Controller still owns what reaches the board. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst’s monthly view of absence and headcount, used as aggregate hours and cost. The analyst would need the AFAS absence codes that drive cost, and would leave named sick-leave records and the Wet verbetering poortwachter file with HR.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a one-off, such as a delayed sailing or a short sick wave, from a new run-rate, and knows which site explanation has been reliable before. The forecast should change only when the analyst accepts that reading.
tasks.pattern_why: The trend table is a fixed query, and the note is one pass that turns the variance lines and the site comment into a sourced explanation of what the budget needs. The analyst approves that note inside the same monthly workflow.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract after the period closes, or a mid-month variance over the agreed threshold.
steps: A fixed query builds budget versus actual by site, cost centre and driver.
Lines that do not tie to the general ledger are held out.
One model call drafts the trend note, each sentence pointed at a source line, and states the effect on next quarter.
The analyst accepts, edits or rejects the change in need before it enters the forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: The forecast need changes only after the analyst approves the note. The Controller still decides what is reported to the board.
data_needed: Operating budget and actuals by site and cost centre
Hours, overtime, agency hours and agency rates
Volume
Aggregate absence hours
The prior forecast and the driver definitions
in_practice.logs_to: The note, the query and the prompt, stored with the month-close workpapers on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: In the same finance-executive survey, variance analysis scored a net +28 and forecasting a net +34 for AI usefulness, while data quality was the top barrier at 40.4 percent.
OneStream’s described split has agents flag records that do not tie, do the variance arithmetic and draft commentary, while people decide which source wins.
Without a prepared semantic model, Power BI Copilot can misinterpret the data, and non-English use is not officially supported.
Faster commentary on uncertified numbers makes existing errors harder to catch.

risks: The note can explain noise in clean prose and still leave the driver unchanged for the wrong reason.
Agency-portal hours that do not match AFAS will show up as a trend.
Named absence and reintegration files are out of scope; putting them in the forecast file would breach the AVG.
A monthly need figure can become a target the sites follow before the Finance Director has accepted the forecast.
research_questions: What share of monthly variances repeat a known driver, and what share are one-offs the analyst already understands?
Do hours from the three agency portals tie to AFAS within a tolerance the Controller accepts?
Will a site manager use a monthly need view, or will it sit unopened next to the existing pack?
Can a note in Dutch cite the ledger line it came from, in a form the auditor can re-run?

tasks.short: Check monthly that each site is spending inside its budget.

today.trigger: The bookkeepers finish the payables for the period and the nightly extract contains the closed month.
steps: Pull department and site actuals against budget from Power BI.
Tick material lines, including labour, flex, overtime and transport, back to AFAS.
Mark anything over the control limit and ask the budget holder for the cause.
Record whether the breach is released, moved or stopped, and send the list to the Controller.
drudgery: Ticking the same cost centres by hand every month.
Copying breaches into a separate tracker.
Chasing holders who reply in different formats.
today.time_sinks: The tick-and-chase cycle, especially flex invoices that arrive after the extract has refreshed.

lenses.faster: The full tick of every cost centre disappears. Working the breach list, the holder’s reply and the late agency invoices stays, about two fifths of today’s time on this task.
lenses.autonomous: Closure of the AFAS period and the nightly load start the control. A pass or a breach list is produced with no analyst in the loop. The analyst acts on breaches and on lines that do not tie.
lenses.ambitious: A morning note for night-shift supervisors at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, showing yesterday’s overtime and agency hours against the remaining envelope, would serve a group that today sees only a site total after month end. Demand would grow in peak season if the note was trusted, and it can only be as fresh as the nightly extract and the invoices already posted.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking the lines that are inside tolerance. The analyst wants the conversation about a real overspend and whether to stop the rest of the month.
lenses.options: On a breach the holder can absorb it, draw contingency, or cut the remaining weeks. Those three leave the site with different forecasts and a different cash picture for the Controller.
lenses.altitude: During the close the week is the breach list. The analyst gains the right to hold a cost centre over the agreed tolerance until the holder explains it. The job becomes more expert on the exceptions.
reach: The bookkeeper’s check that a flex or other operating invoice carries a cost centre before it is posted. The analyst would need the AFAS coding rules and the match the bookkeepers already run.

tasks.human_edge: The rule can find a breach. The analyst knows whether the board has already accepted that peak, and whether the hours have already been worked under the CAO and cannot be pulled back.
tasks.pattern_why: Expenditure control here is a written comparison of budget, actual and tolerance, plus a list of lines that fail or do not tie. That can be coded and run on the extract with no model.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS period is closed and the nightly extract has loaded.
steps: A check compares actual with budget by cost centre and site, using the tolerances stored with the budget procedure.
Lines that do not tie to the ledger are sent to the bookkeeper and left out of the pass.
Breaches are listed with the amount, the holder and the remaining envelope.
The analyst records release, move or stop on that list only.
in_practice.human_gate: A clean pass needs no approval. A breach is released, and the forecast is changed, only after the analyst records a decision. Amounts above the Controller’s limit go to the Controller.
data_needed: Budget and actual by cost centre and site
The written tolerances and the cost-centre owner
Open commitments where AFAS already holds them
Agency invoices that are posted, and a marker for those still missing
in_practice.logs_to: The control log on SharePoint, stored with the month-close file.

evidence.claim: Described FP&A agents flag records that do not tie and do the variance arithmetic; people keep the decisions that go to the board.
Variance analysis is reported as a strong use of AI, net +28, and data quality is the top barrier at 40.4 percent.
A vendor launching finance agents states that in payroll and finance a good guess is not good enough.
Encoded policies are a precondition; speed otherwise repeats errors already in the file.

risks: Tolerances that are too tight flood the close; tolerances that are too loose miss a real overspend.
A flex invoice posted next period can turn a pass into a miss after the pack has gone.
Hours already worked on a shift cannot be uncontrolled by a finance flag, and a stop has to respect the CAO.
The check should stay on money and cost centres. Scoring or ranking named staff would pull it toward worker monitoring and an AVG question.
research_questions: In a typical month, how many cost-centre lines sit inside tolerance, and how many breaches does the Controller actually discuss?
How often is a breach a flex or payables invoice that posts in the next period?
Are the tolerances written down, and who may change them?
Do night-shift supervisors see any budget figure today?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions for missing lines, bad figures and broken rules.

today.trigger: A site or a department files a budget or a reforecast, or the annual calendar reaches review week.
steps: Check that every cost centre, the flex assumption and the volume driver are present.
Recalculate labour from CAO scales, overtime percentages and the agency rate.
Compare the file with the procedure and template on SharePoint.
Send the missing lines and the figures that do not match AFAS actuals back to the manager and the Controller.
drudgery: Repeating the same completeness ticks on each site file.
Hunting last year’s workbook to see which layout was accepted.
Chasing sheets that nobody has signed.
today.time_sinks: Submissions that arrive in a local Excel layout, and labour maths that each site calculates in its own way.

lenses.faster: The template tick, the completeness list and the labour recalculation disappear. Review of the fails, and of a pack that passes and is still undeliverable, stays at about two fifths of today’s check.
lenses.autonomous: Saving a submission in the SharePoint budget folder starts the check. Pass or fail is returned with no analyst in the loop. The analyst sees the fails, and a technical pass still waits for the budget to be accepted later.
lenses.ambitious: Running the same check on every mid-year reforecast in peak, including Venlo and the night operation, would make a decision that today happens once a year. Demand would grow if the check was cheap, because sites currently avoid a resubmission that takes a week to review.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking templates and re-adding overtime. The analyst wants the submission that is complete and still wrong in a way the procedure does not mention.
lenses.options: A fail on the agency rate can be repaired with the contracted rate, with a new rate from procurement, or with fewer hours. Those repairs are different budgets, and the Controller’s response changes with which one is inside the envelope.
lenses.altitude: In budget season the week is failed submissions and gaps in the procedure. The analyst gains the right to send a pack back when a coded check fails, and proposes a procedure change to the Controller when a pass is still wrong. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist’s check that budgeted hourly rates match the current CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO. The analyst would need the scales, the allowances, and the date a wage round takes effect.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can see a submission that passes every tick and still cannot be staffed, including a straight rollover of last year’s pad. Unusual works-council or CAO cases stay with the person because the procedure does not cover them.
tasks.pattern_why: Completeness, arithmetic and a written procedure are pass or fail rules. They can be coded against the template, the CAO parameters and the AFAS actuals. A model is unnecessary for a missing cost centre or an overtime rate above the parameter file.

in_practice.trigger: A budget file lands in the SharePoint submission folder.
steps: The check looks for required cost centres, drivers, signature fields and the current template version.
It recalculates labour and flex against the CAO and agency parameters stored with the procedure.
It matches opening figures to the last closed AFAS actuals and flags a submission that copies last year unchanged.
The analyst reviews the fail list and either sends it back or forwards a technical pass.
in_practice.human_gate: A fail goes back to the manager and does not enter the budget. The analyst accepts technical conformance only. The Finance Director still approves the budget.
data_needed: The current submission template and the cost-centre list
CAO wage parameters and allowances used in the budget
The agency rate card
Last closed actuals
The written budget procedure and the rule version
in_practice.logs_to: The check result stored beside the submission on SharePoint, with the rule version that was used.

evidence.claim: Agents do not supply missing clean data, certified reports, defined drivers or encoded policies, and speed makes old errors harder to catch.
Described FP&A agents flag records that do not tie, and people decide which source wins.
Budgeting is where surveyed finance executives most often found AI more useful than expected, while tasks that demand judgement were the least successful.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

risks: A parameter file that lags the new CAO wage table will pass a labour cost that is already wrong.
Flagging every unchanged line will punish a site that genuinely has no change, and managers will start adding noise.
An arithmetic pass can be mistaken for conformance with the works council’s process.
Submissions that name people and salaries need to be sent back; that pay data belongs in AFAS.
research_questions: Is the budget procedure on SharePoint specific enough to turn into pass or fail rules?
What share of submissions fail on missing lines and arithmetic, and what share fail on a judgement the Controller still has to make?
Who updates CAO rates in the budget file when a wage round lands, and how many weeks late is that update?
Do technical passes reduce later audit adjustments, or do the same errors still appear at close?

tasks.short: Calculate what a site project or peak season will cost.

today.trigger: A site manager, customer-operations lead or the Finance Director asks what a project, a new shift or a customer peak will take to run.
steps: Collect AFAS actuals for a similar activity: labour, flex, overtime, transport and materials.
Ask the site or HR for hours and whether own staff or agency flex will do the work.
Build the cost stack in Excel and note the missing drivers.
Compare the total with the site envelope and write the assumptions for the Controller.
drudgery: Hunting an old workbook for a comparable cost centre.
Rebuilding the same cost stack from scratch.
Asking again for a driver the site has already sent.
today.time_sinks: Finding a comparable that is actually similar, and waiting for the site to confirm the hours.

lenses.faster: Searching for comparables and drafting the first cost stack disappear. Agreeing the hours with the site and accepting the comparable stay, and the wait for the site is still about half the elapsed time. About two fifths of the hours disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A request with site, dates and volume starts the draft. The draft is produced without the analyst assembling it. It counts only after the analyst approves the comparable and the hours.
lenses.ambitious: A sourced cost for customer-operations before they accept a peak above an agreed volume, at each of the three sites, would be a new service. They do not get it today unless the Finance Director already knows about the peak. Demand would grow if the answer was cheap, because peaks are now accepted or refused on a guess.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the search through old workbooks. The analyst wants the argument about whether the comparable is fair and what the site would give up.
lenses.options: Own staff on overtime, agency flex, and a smaller volume produce different costs, different CAO overtime and different certificate constraints. The go or no-go changes with that mix.
lenses.altitude: The week includes a short queue of project estimates. The analyst gains the right to state the resource figure the company will use for that request. The Controller still accepts anything that moves the site envelope. The job becomes more expert on comparables.
reach: The Recruiter’s first sizing of how many flex workers a peak needs, expressed as hours and cost. The analyst would need agency order lead times and certificate constraints such as forklift and VCA, as counts of qualified people.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the comparable, and refusing one that mixes a Venlo night peak with a Rotterdam day shift, is the analyst’s call. A model will average unlike activities if it is allowed to pick the source itself.
tasks.pattern_why: The request arrives as a messy note, and the output is a sourced estimate in a fixed template. One model call can draft that from the comparables. The analyst approves the figure before anyone relies on it.

in_practice.trigger: A project or peak request is logged with volume, site, dates and the name of the internal customer.
steps: The workflow pulls comparable actuals by site and activity from the AFAS extract.
One model call drafts hours, labour, flex, other cost and the gap against the envelope, each figure tied to a source.
The same draft costs the overtime mix, the agency mix and the smaller-volume mix.
The analyst checks the comparable and either issues the figure or sends the draft back.
in_practice.human_gate: The figure goes to the site or to customer-operations only after the analyst approves it. A budget transfer still waits for the Controller.
data_needed: Comparable cost centres and activity actuals
Requested volume, site and dates
CAO overtime parameters and the agency rate card
Remaining site envelope
Counts of people who hold the certificates the work requires
in_practice.logs_to: The note, the sources and the prompt in the project folder on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Surveyed finance executives reported net usefulness of +34 for forecasting, +27 for model building and +26 for scenario planning.
Described FP&A agents gather data and run scenario mechanics; people decide which source wins and allocate the money.
Defined drivers are a precondition, or the draft costs the wrong thing faster.
Power BI Copilot needs a prepared semantic model and can misinterpret data that has not been prepared.

risks: A comparable from the wrong site produces a confident cost that the operation cannot hit.
Training records are personal data. The estimate can use counts of certificate holders, and named Studytube records stay with Learning and Development.
The figure can be read as permission to hire flex. Structural staffing changes still go through the works council.
A cheap answer invites more requests, and the analyst’s review queue becomes the bottleneck. The Pigment survey found the most AI-mature teams spending more hours on executive reporting.
research_questions: How many project and peak requests arrive in a quarter, and how many receive a full cost today?
Does AFAS hold activity actuals that are comparable, or only site cost centres that mix several kinds of work?
Would customer-operations send more requests if the answer came back in a day, and does the Controller want that queue?
Which constraints, CAO hours, agency notice or certificates, change the cost enough to belong in the first draft?

tasks.short: Summarise a request for extra budget and recommend a decision.

today.trigger: A manager asks by mail or in a meeting for extra budget or for a transfer between cost centres.
steps: Read the request and look up the remaining budget in Power BI or AFAS.
Check the site envelope, the contingency and what is already committed.
Write a one-page summary with a yes, a no, or a yes with conditions.
Send it to the Controller and the Finance Director, then record the decision and update the forecast if it was approved.
drudgery: Rewriting the same one-pager for every request.
Looking up the remaining budget by hand.
Filing the mail thread so the decision can be found at the next close.
today.time_sinks: Requests that arrive with no cost, and reconstructing what was already approved this quarter.

lenses.faster: Looking up the envelope and writing the one-pager disappear. The recommendation and the conversation with the Controller stay, about half the hours on this task.
lenses.autonomous: A mail to the finance inbox or a SharePoint form starts the draft memo. The draft is written with no analyst at the keyboard. It is submitted only after the analyst signs it, and the money moves only after the Finance Director decides.
lenses.ambitious: A recommendation on flex and overtime requests above a set amount from night-shift supervisors would decide the money when the shift is being planned, for a group that today spends first and explains at month end. Demand would grow if it was cheap, so the threshold has to keep small lines on the cost centre.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching for the remaining budget and reformatting the memo. The analyst wants the recommendation, especially the conditional yes.
lenses.options: Approving in full, approving from contingency, or refusing and offering a smaller scope leave the site with different forecasts. The Director’s decision changes when those three sit next to the remaining envelope.
lenses.altitude: The week has a decision queue. The analyst gains the right to send back a request that has no cost or no budget line, and to recommend no. The Finance Director still approves the money. The job becomes more expert on the recommendation.
reach: The Controller’s write-up of funds requests under a written threshold. The analyst would need the list of items the Finance Director always takes to the board and the bank, such as a lease or a customer penalty.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst has to make the recommendation and stand behind the precedent it sets for the other two sites. A promise already made to a customer or to the works council is something the analyst knows and the draft does not.
tasks.pattern_why: The request is an unstructured mail, and the company always needs the same memo: what is asked, what remains, what is committed, and a recommendation. One model call can draft it. The steps do not vary, and a person decides before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: A funds request arrives by mail or on a SharePoint form.
steps: The request is logged and the remaining site and cost-centre budget is read from the extract.
One model call drafts a one-page memo with the ask, the remaining envelope, the open commitments and three options.
The analyst edits the recommendation and signs the memo.
The memo goes to the Controller or the Finance Director according to the written threshold, and the forecast updates only after that decision.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every memo before it is submitted. The Controller or the Finance Director approves or refuses the money. The analyst does not release budget in AFAS.
data_needed: The request text
Remaining budget and the contingency balance
Open commitments
Written approval thresholds
Decisions on similar requests this year
in_practice.logs_to: The memo, the source figures and the decision, stored on SharePoint and attached to the month’s forecast file.

evidence.claim: In the described FP&A split, agents draft commentary and people allocate capital and face the board.
Tasks that demand human judgement were the least successful use of AI in the finance survey, and the benefit that rose was accuracy and confidence in planning outcomes, at 49.7 percent.
Commentary written after the number does not repair a weak request, a rollover or a padded line.
A memo pasted from a personal chatbot cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

risks: A fluent memo can recommend yes because the incoming mail was confident.
At higher volume the analyst’s signature can become a rubber stamp on a draft they did not really review.
Thresholds copied from habit will harden into policy the Finance Director never set.
A refusal that changes staffing can be a works-council matter, and the memo has to say so before it looks like a final labour decision.
research_questions: How many funds requests arrive in a month, of what size, and how many are approved?
Are approval thresholds written down, and do they match what the Finance Director wants to see personally?
What share of requests arrive with no cost or no budget line?
Does a faster memo change the decision, or only the waiting time?

tasks.short: Get the monthly budget pack out and handle one-off board reports.

today.trigger: The month-close calendar calls for the regular pack, or the Finance Director asks for a special report for the board or the bank.
steps: Ask the bookkeepers and the other analyst for the cuts and the deadline.
Pull the standard site and cost-centre views from Power BI and finish them in Excel.
Write the commentary and chase numbers that are still missing.
Assemble the pack for the Controller. For a special, build a new cut and explain it.
drudgery: Chasing the same cuts every month.
Pasting Power BI visuals into slides.
Working out which file is the pack the Controller has.
today.time_sinks: The regular pack is a production calendar. A special blows the calendar up because it is built from a blank sheet.

lenses.faster: Chasing and assembling the regular pack disappear. Releasing it, writing the few lines that matter, and building specials stay. Those remaining pieces are about three fifths of today’s hours, so about two fifths disappear.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar starts the regular pack once the closed period is in the nightly extract. The agreed pages refresh without the analyst chasing them. The pack is sent only when the analyst releases it, and a special starts only when the Finance Director asks.
lenses.ambitious: A fixed monthly pack for the three warehouse managers, in a form they can use, would be a new service beside the company pack for the Finance Director. Demand would grow if it was cheap. The survey evidence says the most AI-mature teams already spend more hours on executive reporting, so the page list has to stay fixed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing pages and pasting charts. The analyst wants the special that answers a real board question, and the commentary on the two numbers that matter.
lenses.options: The regular pack carries the agreed scenarios every month, so a new layout does not create a new decision. A special on a late peak still needs two or three cuts, because the cut changes what the board concludes.
lenses.altitude: The regular cycle becomes a release slot inside the close. The analyst gains the right to refuse a new recurring report that is off the agreed list. The Finance Director still decides what the board sees. The job becomes more expert on specials.
reach: The Controller’s assembly of the monthly management pack. The analyst would need the close timetable and the adjustments only the Controller is willing to describe. The Controller keeps the sign-off on the numbers.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell what the board is asking this month, including when the question is the bank or a loss at one site, and can refuse to release a pack they have not read. The refresh can assemble the agreed pages and cannot make that call.
tasks.pattern_why: The regular pack is the same pages from the same nightly extract, so a refresh and a tie-out can run without a model. Specials, and the sentences around the numbers, stay with the analyst as the exception they handle before release.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar reaches the regular pack, or the Finance Director names a special.
steps: After the period is closed, the agreed pages refresh from the semantic model.
Pages that do not tie to AFAS are held out of the pack.
The analyst reviews the pack, edits the short commentary and releases it.
A special is scoped with the Finance Director, and the analyst builds it from a pulled cut.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases the regular pack. The Controller or the Finance Director accepts it for the board. A special goes out only through the analyst.
data_needed: The agreed page list and the certified measures
A tie-out to the general ledger
The sources behind the commentary
The board calendar
in_practice.logs_to: The released pack and the model version, stored on SharePoint with the close file.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can summarise reports and write DAX on Fabric F2+ or Premium. Without preparation it can misinterpret the data, and non-English use is not officially supported.
The most AI-mature finance teams in the Pigment survey spend more hours on executive reporting, and reduced manual work has fallen as a reported benefit every quarter.
OneStream states cycle-time reductions above 82 percent for its forecast product and names no customer. It also says the week was rearranged and the team was not smaller.
Faster reports on numbers that are not certified spread errors that were already there.

risks: A shorter production cycle can fill up with new packs and leave days to close unchanged.
Dutch cost-centre names will be misread if commentary is left to Copilot on an unprepared model.
A pack that does not tie to AFAS creates audit adjustments, which is one of the team’s input metrics.
Commentary written after the number, in cleaner sentences, still leaves a weak forecast looking finished.
research_questions: How many hours a month go to the regular pack, and how many to specials?
Is there a certified semantic model today, or is every pack still finished in Excel?
Which pages does the Finance Director use in the board meeting?
If the regular pack is ready earlier, does the close get shorter, or do new specials fill the time?

tasks.short: Match project and cost-centre budgets to the site, including contingency.

today.trigger: A budget version is being assembled, a transfer is requested, or someone wants to draw contingency for overtime, damage, a sudden peak or a similar event.
steps: List project and cost-centre budgets and add them to the site total.
Check that the three site totals add up to the company budget.
Identify the contingency line and what has already been drawn.
Propose the match or the transfer in Excel, and wait for the Controller before AFAS is updated.
drudgery: Adding hierarchies that break when a cost centre has no parent.
Keeping a side list of contingency draws that never makes it back to the budget file.
Reconciling three workbooks that use different codes.
today.time_sinks: Finding why the sum of the parts is not the site total.

lenses.faster: Adding up the hierarchy and hunting the difference disappear. Classifying a contingency draw that fits no listed type, and waiting for the Controller, stay. A bit under half the hours on this task disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new budget version or a contingency request starts the tie-out. Gaps are listed with no analyst in the loop. A clean match can be offered as the version to load, and nothing posts to AFAS until the Controller agrees.
lenses.ambitious: A morning balance of the site reserve for the night shift and the peak operation, so they can see what is left before they place agency orders, would serve shifts that today meet the reserve only after the fact. Demand would grow in peak if the balance was cheap and current. With a nightly extract it is a morning figure, and it is only as good as the draws already recorded.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing a difference across three files. The analyst wants the few draws that are real emergencies, and the decision on whether the reserve is the right size.
lenses.options: Funding a peak from contingency, from unused lines inside the site, or from next month’s flex budget leaves a different reserve and a different rest of the year. The Controller’s decision changes with which source is used. A plug that forces the totals to agree removes that choice.
lenses.altitude: The week shows breaks in the hierarchy and movements in the reserve. The analyst gains the right to block a version that does not tie, and to propose the reserve level for the year. The Controller authorises a draw above the limit. The job becomes more expert on the reserve.
reach: The bookkeeper’s mapping of a new general-ledger account to a cost centre and a site. The analyst would need the AFAS chart of accounts and the practice that the Controller names the parent before the account is used.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a real emergency from a budget miss that someone wants the reserve to absorb, and can say what the reserve should be. The tie-out should show the gap and should not invent a plug.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching cost centre to site and site to company is a hierarchy and a tie-out. Once contingency types and limits are listed, the draw is a rule as well. Both can run without a model. A draw that fits no type is the exception the analyst handles.

in_practice.trigger: A new budget version is saved, or a contingency draw is requested.
steps: The check rolls cost centres and projects to sites and to the company on the hierarchy table.
Any gap is listed with the missing parent and the amount.
Draws of a listed type reduce that site’s reserve; a draw with no type is set aside.
The analyst reviews the gaps and the untyped draws, then sends a clean version to the Controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst can refuse a version that does not tie. No hierarchy change and no contingency draw is posted in AFAS until the Controller approves it.
data_needed: The cost-centre to site to company map
Project codes
Contingency types, limits and draws year to date
The budget version being matched
in_practice.logs_to: The tie-out report and the Controller’s approval, stored with that budget version on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Described FP&A agents do variance arithmetic and flag records that do not tie, while people allocate the money.
Without encoded policies, speed repeats the old plug, the rollover and the padded line.
Model building scored a net +27 for AI usefulness in the finance survey, and data quality was the top barrier at 40.4 percent.
At Noordhaven the public-sector wording, appropriations and emergency funds, reads as cost-centre and site budgets plus a contingency. The board and the bank are the audience.

risks: A script that plugs the difference will hide the miss the analyst currently finds by hand.
Using contingency for structural flex will empty the reserve before a real incident.
Drawing the reserve to avoid a staffing decision can go around the works council.
If the AFAS parent map is wrong, every clean match is wrong with it. Data quality is the known barrier.
research_questions: Does AFAS already hold a cost-centre to site hierarchy that ties to the general ledger, or is the match done only in Excel?
How often do the parts fail to add to the site, and what causes the gap?
What was contingency used for in the last year, and how much of it was a real emergency?
Who may draw the reserve today, and is that limit written down?

role.altitude: The two analysts move from assembling workbooks and packs to keeping the driver definitions, the control tolerances and the forecast rules, and to working the exception queue with the three sites. They gain the right to send a submission back, to hold a cost centre over tolerance, to state a project figure, and to refuse a recurring report that is off the agreed list. The Controller and the Finance Director still accept the budget, release money and face the board and the bank. The job becomes more expert. The test is forecast accuracy and days to close.
reach: The Controller’s first-pass review of site submissions and the assembly of the monthly management pack, with the Controller keeping the sign-off.
The bookkeepers’ first check that a flex invoice or a new ledger account has a cost centre and a site parent, with posting staying in accounts payable and receivable.
The Compensation and Benefits Specialist’s check that budgeted rates match the current CAO scales, with CAO negotiations staying there.
The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst’s aggregate absence and headcount, used as cost drivers, with named records and the Wet verbetering poortwachter file staying in HR.
The Recruiter’s first sizing of peak flex in hours and cost, with the hiring decision and the agency order staying in talent acquisition.
role.ceiling_note: Two people at a loaded EUR 80 an hour can review breaches, funds requests, specials and conversations with three sites. They cannot review every flex order or every night shift. Anything still outside the nightly AFAS extract, including agency portals, a request with no cost, and a hierarchy that exists only in Excel, stays slow. The works council, the two CAOs and the Finance Director’s signature limit which choices finance can make alone. A faster pack that does not tie adds audit adjustments and can make the close longer.
skills_to_grow: Writing driver definitions, tolerances and contingency types so a check can run without them in the loop.
Reading an AFAS trial balance and a cost-centre hierarchy well enough to refuse a version that does not tie.
CAO wage and overtime parameters at the level needed to test a budget, and knowing when a labour change needs the works council.
Keeping forecast files to aggregate headcount so the AVG line on named people stays intact.
Filing workpapers on SharePoint so an auditor can rebuild the figure.
The month-close calendar, and which pages the board pack is allowed to contain.
role.ambitious_version: Each month the analysts run a rolling forecast and a small set of scenarios for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, including the flex band, on drivers the site managers accept. Customer-operations receives a sourced cost before a peak is accepted. The close, the site conversations and the board pack use the same figures. The week is rearranged around those decisions, and the team stays two people. It is worth doing only if forecast accuracy improves and days to close fall. If the drivers are not defined first, the company gets a faster copy of the old budget.
